claims.statement: The `apps/mercato/` Next.js App Router app is the main runtime: it exposes catch-all dispatchers (`app/api/[...slug]/route.ts`, `app/(backend)/backend/[...slug]/page.tsx`, `app/(frontend)/[...slug]/page.tsx`), declares module enablement in `src/modules.ts`, and bootstraps server foundation data (modules, entities, DI registrars, generated registries) via `src/bootstrap-common.ts` and `src/bootstrap.ts`/`src/bootstrap-api.ts`.

`apps/mercato/src/modules.ts` exports `enabledModules`, the ordered list of `{ id, from, overrides? }` entries that wire every module to its package (`@open-mercato/core`, `@app`, `@open-mercato/search`, `@open-mercato/scheduler`, provider packages, etc.); user-created modules live in `src/modules/` under the `@app` alias.

App-only modules in `modules.ts` are `example` (reference module, disabled by default — uncomment its entry to re-enable), `example_customers_sync` (auto-pushed only while `example` is present), and `ratelimit_probe` (lightweight rate-limit endpoint probe from `@app`).

Enterprise modules are gated by env flags parsed in `modules.ts`: `OM_ENABLE_ENTERPRISE_MODULES=true` adds `record_locks` and `system_status_overlays`; `OM_ENABLE_ENTERPRISE_MODULES_SSO=true` adds `sso`; `OM_ENABLE_ENTERPRISE_MODULES_SECURITY=true` adds `security`; all from `@open-mercato/enterprise`.
`storage_s3` is conditionally enabled only when `OM_ENABLE_STORAGE_S3` is truthy, pushing `{ id: 'storage_s3', from: '@open-mercato/storage-s3' }` onto `enabledModules`.

`apps/docs/` is a Docusaurus site (package `open-mercato-docs`) published to `docs.open-mercato.dev`, using `@docusaurus/theme-mermaid` for diagrams and `@easyops-cn/docusaurus-search-local` for local search; configured by `docusaurus.config.ts`/`sidebars.ts` and deployed via `vercel.json`.

The repo is a Yarn 4 workspaces monorepo (`packageManager: yarn@4.17.1`, Node 24) with workspaces `apps/*`, `packages/*`, and `external/official-modules/packages/*`; package names use the `@open-mercato/*` scope and `create-mercato-app` for the scaffolder.

`packages/shared` (`@open-mercato/shared`) holds cross-cutting utilities with zero domain dependencies: CRUD factory + optimistic-lock helpers, DI container (`createRequestContainer`), i18n, RBAC feature matching, encryption-with-decryption, module event declarations (`createModuleEvents`), Standard Webhooks sign/verify primitives, and SSRF URL-safety guards.

`packages/core` (`@open-mercato/core`) is the largest package, containing 40+ business modules under `src/modules/` (auth, directory, customers, catalog, sales, wms, workflows, communication_channels, push_notifications, etc.), each following the standard module convention; it is documented by `AGENTS.md` and the per-module directories.

`packages/ui` (`@open-mercato/ui`) exports the backend admin UI and design-system components (AppShell, Page, DataTable, CrudForm, RowActions, dashboard, messages) from `src/index.ts`, plus frontend Layout/AuthFooter/LanguageSwitcher, primitives (buttons, inputs, spinner), and AI record card types from `src/ai`.

`packages/ai-assistant` (`@open-mercato/ai-assistant`) provides the AI chat backend and MCP server: it exports `defineAiAgent`/`defineAiTool`/`registerMcpTool`, runs an MCP HTTP server (default port 3001) via `mcp:serve`/`mcp:dev`, and houses Code Mode tools + scope-injection in `src/modules/ai_assistant/lib/`.

`packages/search` (`@open-mercato/search`) bundles three strategies — TokenSearchStrategy (encrypted data), VectorSearchStrategy (embeddings via `src/vector/`), and FullTextSearchStrategy (pluggable Meilisearch/Algolia drivers) — exposed through `SearchService` and a search module under `src/modules/search/`.

`packages/events` (`@open-mercato/events`) is the event bus backbone: it dispatches ephemeral (inline) and persistent (queued via `@open-mercato/queue`) subscribers, supports `clientBroadcast`/`crossProcessBroadcast` events bridged across processes via PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY, and keeps persistent subscribers durable across restarts.

`packages/queue` (`@open-mercato/queue`) provides a unified job-queue API with two strategies — local (file-based under `.mercato/queue/`) and async (BullMQ/Redis with retries) — plus a worker contract (`metadata = { queue, id?, concurrency? }`); the DB connection budget invariant `web_pool_max + worker_pool_max + scheduler/overhead ≤ Postgres max_connections` must hold.

`packages/cache` (`@open-mercato/cache`) provides tenant-scoped caching with four strategies — memory (default, LRU-bounded, default 50000 entries tunable via `CACHE_MEMORY_MAX_ENTRIES`), SQLite, Redis, and JSON file — plus tag-based invalidation; cache invalidation fires post-commit after `withAtomicFlush`.

`packages/scheduler` (`@open-mercato/scheduler`) is a standalone module package (not under `packages/core`) enabled in `modules.ts` via `{ id: 'scheduler', from: '@open-mercato/scheduler' }`; it manages database-backed scheduled jobs (cron/interval, queue/command targets, next-run tracking) through `SchedulerService`/`BullMQSchedulerService`/`LocalSchedulerService`, depending on `@open-mercato/queue` and `@open-mercato/shared`.

`packages/telemetry` (`@open-mercato/telemetry`) is vendor-neutral telemetry (spans, metrics, error reporting, shared-logger bridge) that is OFF by default: `initTelemetry()` only starts a provider when `TELEMETRY_BACKEND` resolves to non-`noop`; OTLP backends `signoz`/`newrelic`/`otlp` share one dynamically-loaded exporter differing only by endpoint+headers, and `@opentelemetry/*` is imported solely by `src/provider/otlp-provider.ts`.

`packages/eslint-plugin-ds` (`@open-mercato/eslint-plugin-ds`) is a private structural ESLint plugin enforcing the design system with seven rules (all at `warn` during rollout): `require-empty-state`, `require-page-wrapper`, `no-raw-table`, `require-loading-state`, `require-status-badge`, `no-hardcoded-status-colors`, and `no-legacy-alert-variant`; the six backend-structural rules scope to backend globs while `no-legacy-alert-variant` spans `packages/*/src/**/*.tsx` and `apps/*/src/**/*.tsx`, invoked via `yarn lint:ds`.

`packages/cli` (`@open-mercato/cli`) holds code generators and CLI tooling; its binary `packages/cli/dist/bin.js` (invoked as `yarn mercato`) backs AST-based module discovery/generation (`yarn generate` → ~20 generated registries) and MikroORM migration generation (`yarn db:generate`), with `mercato` and `registry` export surfaces.

`packages/onboarding` (`@open-mercato/onboarding`) provides the self-service tenant/organization onboarding flow — setup wizard, deferred provisioning, ready/invitation email flows — enabled in `modules.ts` via `{ id: 'onboarding', from: '@open-mercato/onboarding' }`.

`packages/content` (`@open-mercato/content`) provides static informational content pages (terms of service, privacy policy) via a `content` module enabled in `modules.ts` from `@open-mercato/content`.

`packages/create-app` (`create-mercato-app`) is the standalone app scaffolder run via `npx create-mercato-app` (binary `./bin/create-mercato-app`), mirroring `apps/mercato/` into a template and keeping them in sync via the root `template:sync` script.

Communication-channel provider packages (channel-apns/expo/fcm/gmail/imap) register a `ChannelAdapter` at import time via `setup.ts` into the Communications Hub's adapter-registry singleton, keyed by `providerKey` (e.g. `apns` for Apple Push); the hub routes each device/message by matching `providerKey`.

Integration provider packages are dedicated npm workspaces (`gateway-stripe`, `channel-*`, `storage-s3`, `sync-akeneo`, `checkout`, `documents`, `webhooks`) that MUST NOT be placed inside `packages/core/src/modules/`; each is enabled as a `ModuleEntry` in `modules.ts` from its `@open-mercato/*` import.

`packages/documents` (`@open-mercato/documents`) is the collaborative internal-documents module (TipTap + Yjs) with a Hocuspocus WebSocket sidecar at `server/documents-collab-server.ts` (started by `yarn documents:collab` / `collab:prod`), requiring `auth`, `directory`, and `attachments` and enabled in `modules.ts` from `@open-mercato/documents`.

`packages/webhooks` (`@open-mercato/webhooks`) implements outbound/inbound webhooks with Standard Webhooks signing/verification (from `@open-mercato/shared/lib/webhooks`), delivery queues/workers, and an adapter registry re-exported from `src/index.ts`.

`packages/enterprise` (`@open-mercato/enterprise`) is commercial proprietary software with its own license (`LICENSE.md`/`TERMS.md`) that accepts no external PRs (per `CONTRIBUTING.md`); its modules (`record_locks`, `system_status_overlays`, `sso`, `security`) are activated only via the env flags in `modules.ts`.

The `external/official-modules` git submodule (configured in `official-modules.json` and wired as a Yarn workspace `external/official-modules/packages/*`) is managed by `yarn official-modules`; activated entries are generated into the versioned `apps/mercato/src/official-modules.generated.ts` and appended to `enabledModules` in `modules.ts` (deduped by id).

Root configuration governs the monorepo: `package.json` (Yarn 4 workspaces, Node 24, root scripts), `turbo.json` (task pipeline build/dev/watch/test/lint/typecheck/generate/db:*), `tsconfig.base.json` (shared TS config), `jest.config.base.cjs` (maxWorkers:2, workerIdleMemoryLimit:512MB), `eslint.config.mjs`/`eslint.ds.config.mjs`, `.yarnrc.yml`, `.nvmrc` (24), and Docker compose files (`docker-compose.yml`, `docker-compose.fullapp.yml`, `docker-compose.fullapp.dev.yml`).

`docker-compose.yml` runs base dev services (pgvector/pgvector:pg17-trixie PostgreSQL, Redis 7, Meilisearch v1.11, LocalStack); `docker-compose.fullapp.yml`/`docker-compose.fullapp.dev.yml` are full-app deployments including an `opencode`/MCP service wiring (`OPENCODE_MCP_URL=http://mcp:3001/mcp`); `Dockerfile` (node:24-alpine) and `railway.toml` cover production deployment.

AI/agent infrastructure lives under `.ai/` — `specs/` (spec-first development), `skills/` (repo-local `om-*` skills), `agentic.config.json` (base branch `develop`, validation commands, pipeline labels, QA gate), lessons/review-checklist/ds-rules — plus root and per-package `AGENTS.md` guides, with the agentic harness config pinned by `.ai/agentic.config.json`.
